card.title: COLD TRAP
card.text: When an enemy unit attacks, add a SISSI as defender.
card.flavorText: The winter during the Winter War of 1939-40 was extraordinarily harsh, with the Karelian Isthmus experiencing a frigid weather with up to -43°C in January 1940. The Finnish forces maximized the advantages offered by the cold and forested landscape to conduct effective defensive operations and hinder the progress of the Soviet forces. For concealment, Finnish soldiers adopted layered clothing, while ski troopers wore lightweight white snow capes, effectively rendering themselves nearly invisible for executing guerrilla tactics against Soviet units. The Finnish forces ensured their comfort and hygiene in the harsh winter conditions by providing warm tents and dugouts with heating from hot stoves. They also had the luxury of saunas to keep them warm and to maintain their personal cleanliness. In contrast, the Soviets dug snow holes which were their main shelters, their tanks were painted in standard olive drab and the troops wore conventional khaki uniforms. They didn’t adapt to the winter environment until late January 1940, when they started painting their equipment white and distributing snowsuits to their infantry.
